Published a standalone MoorePenrose package depending on mathlib4:

https://github.com/KryptosAI/lean-moore-penrose

Defines IsMoorePenroseInverse (heterogeneous, works for non-square matrices) and constructs the pseudo-inverse for RCLike fields via ker(f)ᗮ ≃ₗ range(f). Proves uniqueness, involution (A⁺)⁺ = A, commutation with conjugate transpose (Aᴴ)⁺ = (A⁺)ᴴ, and consistency with the ordinary inverse for invertible matrices.

Originally submitted as PR #36889. The scaffolding was positively reviewed ("looks good" — vihdzp) but the proof style wasn't ready. Published as a standalone package following mathlib4's recommendation for projects outside maintainer expertise.

Available immediately via lake. Happy to work toward eventual mathlib4 inclusion if there's interest.

William Weishuhn said:

("looks good" — vihdzp)

Might want to also state the first part of @Violeta Hernández 's comment though.

It did also say

I won't explicitly vouch for this PR

so that selective inclusion/exclusion of details I think is a bit misleading!

Fair point, thanks for flagging that. Violeta's full comment was: "I won't explicitly vouch for this PR, but I think most of the scaffolding here looks good, and it's just the proofs that could be cleaned up a bit."

That's actually the reason I published it as a standalone package rather than resubmitting to mathlib4 — the proofs need genuine human rework and I'm not a Lean expert. The standalone approach follows mathlib4's own guidance for projects outside maintainer expertise (https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html#what-to-contribute-to-mathlib).

If anyone here with stronger Lean skills is interested in helping clean up the proofs, I'd welcome the collaboration. The mathematical content is correct — it compiles and passes CI.

I have been known ( very very locally so) to voluntarily comb through AI code just for nonsensical Lean code aesthetics and Mathlib optimisation, when it really is not pragmatically needed.

Though I am not sure I’ve ever done this for Mathlib itself yet , I think this is actually rather rare to even happen — AI to legit and mathematically significant Mathlib PR pipeline is real rare so it wouldn’t even be anything specific to this one.

I cannot claim “stronger” lean than you as I know little of you , but , maybe me is the best you’d get as the actual lean experts are very busy.

That would be amazing. I've been chipping away at the proofs since posting — got ker(A⁺) = ker(Aᴴ), rank(A⁺) = rank(A), and pulled the projection identities into their own lemmas. The construction proof in Basic.lean and the conjTranspose lemma still need a human touch though. The logic is fine, the style is what got it flagged.

If you're into it just fork the repo and poke around. Even a second opinion on naming would help. Happy to talk through the math whenever.

No worries, yet you'll find AI can often fill proofs, or even state and fill them with a good natural language source to translate.

But it does so in a vacuum , and iteratively, leading to ballooning of LoC and lack of broader considerations of integration into Mathlib (and just telling it to somehow do it doesn't seem to work, in fact it seems to misunderstand a lot of the metaprogramming parts of Lean, not very interested in reviewing traces effectively to shorten 20 lines with a single tactic).

So for practical purposes its often fine, but for Mathlib AI code still needs a lot of reworking. I will have a look when I can

@Yan Yablonovskiy cleaned up the main proof since your note. it was copy pasting the same setup block as the projection lemmas, took it from ~80 lines to ~45. also swapped out some simp calls that were silently failing for explicit calc. not perfect but a lot less bloated than it was.
